point: The Britannica "French Revolution" snapshot holds only the lead, so the three-estates, bread-price and Tennis Court claims rest on the Wikipedia article and standard content.
The Seven Years War article says nothing of the Stamp Act or British debt, yet is cited beside a claim about them. Is the claim right, and is the ref fair?
The Haitian Revolution article does not mention the Louisiana sale or Haitian help to Bolivar, yet is cited beside those claims.
The Tenement article does not mention the 1901 Tenement House Act, yet is cited beside it.
The Social Darwinism article does not name Carnegie, yet is cited beside a claim about him.
Question 2 option D (a ban on Indian textile imports) is arguable; check that exactly one option is defensible.
Part (c) asks for a change between 1853 and 1909; its scoring notes rest on the Economic history of India and Hind Swaraj articles, and the Hind Swaraj article says nothing about railways.
The 1833 and 1844 factory-law claims cite the Industrial Revolution article; check the dates and what each act did.
Part (c) is a point-of-view question; check it is answerable and its accept list is fair.
